Name: Magnet Cove Titanium Corporation rutile deposit
Notes: Only major rutile deposit known in the area; 5188 short tons of concentrate recovered; controlled by C.H. Scott of Denver in 1952; mill since dismantled; proved to 188 ft by drilling but only shallow weathered material worked

Name: Christy brookite deposit
Notes: 0.5 mi north of Magnet; owned by Malvern Lumber Co in 1952; proved to 130 ft by 21 drill holes plus 1944 test pits; report states no production has been recorded

Name: Kilpatrick brookite deposits (aka Hardy-Walsh)
Notes: 1 mi north of Magnet; owned by the estate of William Kilpatrick in 1952; exploration only test pits and auger holes; no analysis of crystals or concentrate ever made

Name: Mo-Ti Corporation property
Legal_Description: Sec 17 T.3S. R.17W. (south bank of Cove Creek)
Notes: Prospect pit flooded by 1952; rutile-brookite-feldspar veins plus molybdenite cutting perovskite-bearing magnetite-pyroxene rock in drill core; none of this rock crops out at surface

Name: Kimsey calcite quarry area
Legal_Description: West side of Cove Creek, north side of Highway 270
Status: ACTIVE FOR CALCITE - NIOBIUM NEVER PURSUED
Notes: Only good surface exposure of the niobium-bearing carbonatite at Magnet Cove; perovskite with up to 8.8% niobium in single crystals; average grade of the body only about 0.01% niobium

Name: West tufa hill
Legal_Description: North of Kimsey quarry, west of Cove Creek
Notes: Power-auger hole hit only residual clay to surrounding grade; surface littered with iron-stained apatite-rich tufa boulders inferred to derive from underlying calcite rock

Name: Middle tufa hill
Legal_Description: Between west and east tufa hills
Notes: Power auger struck rock at 20 ft and brought up apatite fragments; soil on the flat south of the hill contains abundant magnetite plus some apatite and perovskite

Name: East tufa hill
Legal_Description: North of the church near Kimsey quarry
Notes: Power-auger hole penetrated 40 ft of clay without reaching bedrock (limit of available drill pipe); tufa float less abundant, mixed with bleached igneous rock boulders

Name: Perovskite hill
Legal_Description: Field south of Highway 270, south of the calcite quarry
Notes: Abundant perovskite visible in the soil; named in older reports; no subsurface exploration recorded in the 1954 bulletin

Name: Water well NW corner Sec 19
Notes: A ~90-ft water well penetrated calcite rock; no outcrop nearby but rutile is locally abundant in the surrounding soil

Name: Unnamed perovskite locality east of the magnetite quarry
Legal_Description: ~1000 ft east of the magnetite quarry, north side of Highway 270
Notes: Report states the quantity of perovskite-bearing rock in these localities is not known; paired with the Mo-Ti locality as the only two perovskite-in-silicate-rock occurrences

Name: Wilson prospect
Area: Potash Sulphur Springs (Garland Co, ~6 mi west)
Legal_Description: Hillside east of the hot springs above the Wilson residence
Status: MINIMALLY EXPLORED - FLAGGED FOR MORE WORK
Notes: Confirmed niobium AND uranium in a radioactive boulder (analyzed Dec 1950); only bulldozer trenches plus a single ~75-ft churn-drill hole; report concludes further work should include diamond drilling

Name: Brookite mineralization along Highway 270 at Magnet
Legal_Description: Center of Magnet village at the Y in Highway 270
Status: SOURCE AREA - NOT A DISCRETE CLAIM
Notes: Source of the majority of described brookite specimens from Magnet Cove; quartz veins to 1 in thick with vugs of imperfect quartz and brookite crystals to 5mm; extends ~200 ft up the hill south of the highway

Name: Rutherford Brookite Prospect
Legal_Description: Hill ~400 ft SE of Magnet community
Notes: Elliptical float area 500 ft across centered on a house; smoky quartz in place near the SW corner of the house; compared to the Christy float pattern but smaller; no test pits or drilling ever done

Name: Richardson Rutile Prospect
Notes: Several separated rutile-feldspar veins exposed only along a farm road; plowed field said to be the source of many fine rutile specimens; also an abandoned Civil War-era pyrite shaft with rutile vein material on its dump

Name: York Rutile Prospect
Status: UNTESTED - NO RUTILE FOUND IN PLACE
Notes: Residual rutile aggregates to 1 in common in soil through a farmyard and plowed field; source vein never located; nepheline garnet syenite in the ridge just east is the suspected source

Name: Brookite prospects Section 7 - trenched
Notes: Four now-caved trenches along a low hill's north slope exposed brookite-bearing feldspar veins in metamorphosed Stanley shale

Name: Brookite prospects Section 7 - untested
Notes: Brookite-quartz float over a 20x200 ft area on a ravine slope; report states so far as is known no exploration has been undertaken at this locality

Name: Nichols and Campbell Rutile Prospect
Notes: Produced a small amount of rutile historically; a ~700-ft trench plus gullies still expose rutile-bearing material in the dump; deepest SE end shows rutile masses to 1.5 in

Name: Rutile veins in Section 24
Notes: Feldspar-carbonate veins with fine-grained rutile in a road cut near the Jones Mill aluminum plant road; quantity negligible but demonstrates how widespread the mineralization is

Name: McKnight Placer Rutile Deposit
Notes: Believed sourced from erosion of the main Cove deposits; rutile pebbles to 1 in in a clayey gravel mantle 10-20 ft thick; H.R. McKnight's open pit plus shallow test pits abandoned
